epics.title: Skills overhaul — taxonomy, pattern adoption, multi-mind
epics.description:
A single effort with three threads, all touching the same SKILL.md files: reorganise the 50-plus skills into a broad-to-narrow hierarchy, adopt the Claude Skills patterns Anthropic published, and add the multi-mind affordances needed now that more than one mind is in the fleet. Reference: 'Lessons from Building Claude Code: How We Use Skills', Anthropic, March 2026.

The taxonomy problem: the skill list contains 50-plus narrow, action-specific skills. The UserPromptSubmit hook injects skill names as context, but narrow skills only match when phrasing closely resembles the skill name, so loosely-worded requests bypass skills even when a procedure exists. A hierarchy of broad category skills fixes the match rate. Each level lists five to ten children with one-line descriptions: an agent reads the top-level category, picks a sub-category, reads that, picks a leaf skill, reads that — roughly twenty sentences of context before reaching the actual procedure. Each broad skill self-announces, so route visibility is built in, on the same contract as the skill self-announcement work in the upstream-minds epic.

Five top-level categories. software: code, architecture, system design, building tools, documentation — with sub-categories software/lifecycle for the dev story pipeline from idea to merged PR, and software/tooling for meta-work creating tools, skills, agents and docs. operations: system health, deployments, secrets, memory management, workspace — with operations/system for the running system and infra, operations/memory for the memory lifecycle, graph, vector store and identity, and operations/workspace for the site and canvas. communication: anything sent to a person, service or external platform. planning: stories, schedules, reminders and time management — with planning/project for board management and planning/scheduled for briefings and reminders. information: look things up, fetch data, browse the web.

Note that several leaf skills named in the source taxonomy are since gone or changed: the Planka-backed pipeline skills were orphaned when Planka was torn down 2026-07-30, and the coding skills have been consolidated into one. The taxonomy needs reconciling against what exists before it is built.
epics.requirements:
Five patterns to adopt, each applying to a different subset of skills. context: fork runs a skill in an isolated subagent context so the main conversation is not polluted — for multi-step orchestration with side effects, deep file reads that would bloat context, and skills that spawn sub-skills. Dynamic context injection runs shell commands inside SKILL.md at invocation, injecting output before the skill body is read, so a skill always has current state without asking the model to fetch it. Bundled executable scripts put deterministic steps in Python or shell rather than model reasoning, with the skill invoking the script and the model handling the judgment calls around it. Progressive disclosure keeps SKILL.md lean and references detail files loaded only when needed, applying to any skill over roughly 200 lines. And dynamic HTML output lets a skill bundle scripts that generate interactive charts and visualisations rather than static text.

Implementation order: fix the user-invocable flags first as a fifteen-minute, no-risk pass that changes nothing structural and immediately tidies what surfaces to the user. Then create the five top-level category skills, each announcing itself and listing its sub-categories, with no leaf skill changing yet. Then wire UserPromptSubmit to route via categories, injecting category names instead of raw skill names, and run for a few sessions observing what fires and what misses. Then refine category names and trigger descriptions based on the observed matches. Then apply dynamic context injection to high-traffic skills, context: fork to orchestration skills, bundled scripts to the deterministic ones, and progressive disclosure to the dense ones. Multi-mind affordances last, coordinated with the upstream-minds work, since multi-mind only matters once the containerised minds are on the shared nervous system.
epics.acceptance_criteria: A loosely-worded request reaches the right procedure, which is the match-rate problem the hierarchy exists to solve. Three open questions to settle: whether the top-level category is software or engineering, with software preferred as more concrete; where create-story belongs, since it serves both planning and the software lifecycle and currently sits in software/lifecycle; and whether planning output should route through a web surface so Daniel can review in a browser rather than asking a mind to copy files to a canvas.
epics.qa_tests: Match rate is the measurement, and it is observed rather than asserted: run the category routing for a few sessions and read what fired and what missed. A category whose trigger description does not match real phrasing is refined rather than the design being changed.

features.title: Fix the user-invocable flags
features.description: First, because it is a fifteen-minute pass with no risk and it changes nothing structural.
features.requirements: Seven skills are internal pipeline steps called by other skills and never directly by the user, and should be user-invocable: false — check-reminders, knowledge-graph-save, notify-action, pin-memory-action, planka, secrets and semantic-memory-save. Six are genuinely user-facing utilities and stay true — agent-logs, crypto-price, current-time, reminders, weather and x-search.
features.acceptance_criteria: What surfaces to the user is what the user would ever invoke.
features.qa_tests: Each of the seven is absent from the user-invocable listing and still callable by its parent skill. Each of the six remains present. The planka entry needs reconciling, since Planka was torn down.

stories.title: Set the seven internal pipeline skills to user-invocable: false
stories.description: check-reminders, knowledge-graph-save, notify-action, pin-memory-action, planka, secrets and semantic-memory-save. Called by other skills, never directly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Absent from the user listing, present to their callers.
stories.qa_tests: Each is absent from the user-invocable listing and each parent skill still reaches it.

features.title: The category hierarchy
features.description: Five top-level categories, each listing five to ten children with one-line descriptions, each self-announcing so route visibility is built in.
features.requirements: Create the five category skills — software, operations, communication, planning, information — with their sub-categories: software/lifecycle, software/tooling, operations/system, operations/memory, operations/workspace, planning/project and planning/scheduled. Then wire UserPromptSubmit to inject category names rather than raw skill names, run for a few sessions, and refine the names and trigger descriptions based on what fires and what misses. No leaf skill changes in the first step.
features.acceptance_criteria: Roughly twenty sentences of context before reaching the actual procedure, down from fifty-plus injected skill names.
features.qa_tests: Observed rather than asserted: run the routing and read what fired. A loosely-worded request that previously bypassed a skill should now reach it through its category. Reconcile the leaf lists first — several named skills are gone or consolidated.

stories.title: Create the five top-level category skills
stories.description: software, operations, communication, planning and information, each self-announcing and listing its sub-categories.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Each category announces itself and lists its children.
stories.qa_tests: Invoking a category announces it and lists its sub-categories. A category listing a skill that no longer exists is a reconciliation failure rather than a design one.

stories.title: Route UserPromptSubmit through categories instead of raw skill names
stories.description: Inject category names rather than fifty-plus leaf names, then observe for a few sessions.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A loosely-worded request reaches a procedure.
stories.qa_tests: Run it and read what fired and what missed. The hook must emit hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext rather than systemMessage, which is UI-only and silently never reaches the model.

stories.title: Refine the category names and trigger descriptions from observed matches
stories.description: Step 4. Based on what actually fired.
stories.requirements: Driven by observation rather than by guessing.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The match rate improves measurably.
stories.qa_tests: Compare what fires before and after the refinement on the same kinds of request.

stories.title: Reconcile the leaf skill lists against what exists
stories.description: The taxonomy names Planka-backed pipeline skills orphaned by the 2026-07-30 teardown, and separate planning, coding and review skills since consolidated into one.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No category points at a skill that is gone.
stories.qa_tests: Every skill named in the taxonomy resolves. A category offering a dead skill is worse than an absent category, because nothing on screen says it did nothing.

features.title: Apply context: fork
features.description: Isolation for skills that do complex chained work with side effects, so the main conversation context is not polluted.
features.requirements: Ten candidates, each for a stated reason: code-genius, whose multi-cycle test, code and lint loop pollutes context each cycle; code-review-genius, for deep file reads across many files; master-code-review, which loads a security spec and runs a full review; orchestrator, which spawns sub-skills and manages pipeline state; planning-genius, whose codebase exploration phase is read-heavy; story-close, which goes card to git to rebuild to health check with many side effects; story-start, which spawns planning and manages board state; knowledge-graph-save, for its fuzzy search and disambiguation loop; memory-manager, the parse-classify-route-save pipeline orchestrator; and the nightly autonomous session, which carries the highest risk of context pollution.
features.acceptance_criteria: A forked skill's intermediate work does not reach the main conversation.
features.qa_tests: The forked skill returns its result and not its working. For the orchestration skills the test is that the main conversation's context does not grow by the volume the skill read.

stories.title: Fork the orchestration and review skills
stories.description: code-genius, code-review-genius, master-code-review, orchestrator, planning-genius, story-close and story-start. Several of these have since been consolidated, so apply the pattern to whatever now covers their work.
stories.requirements: Isolated context; result returned as data.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No intermediate file read reaches the main conversation.
stories.qa_tests: The main conversation's context does not grow by the volume the skill read. The skill's conclusion is present.

stories.title: Fork the memory pipeline skills
stories.description: knowledge-graph-save, for its fuzzy search and disambiguation loop, and memory-manager, the parse-classify-route-save orchestrator.
stories.requirements: The disambiguation loop stays out of the conversation.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A memory write does not leave its search results in context.
stories.qa_tests: A write with several fuzzy candidates returns only the outcome.

stories.title: Fork the nightly autonomous session
stories.description: The highest risk of context pollution of any skill.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A nightly run does not leave its working in the next morning's conversation.
stories.qa_tests: After a nightly run, the conversation context carries the run's conclusions rather than its transcript.

features.title: Apply dynamic context injection
features.description: Inject live system state at invocation so a skill has current context without a fetch step.
features.requirements: Fourteen candidates with what each injects: the two briefings get the current date and today's calendar events, with the morning one covering both calendars; sitrep gets the last ten error lines per container plus a memory retrieval for recent system issues; story-close gets the last five commits plus recent container logs; story-start gets the current board state plus the repo file tree; orchestrator gets the board, recent PRs and the last ten commits across all branches; code-genius gets git status plus recent test failures; code-review-genius gets a diff stat and the changed file list; master-code-review gets the detected language and framework plus a diff stat; planning-genius gets the existing tool list and similar file patterns; update-documentation gets the last twenty commits filtered to doc-touching ones; tool-creator gets the stateless and stateful tool listings; x-ai-lurker gets a memory retrieval to seed the report; and semantic-memory-save gets its similarity results pre-fetched.
features.acceptance_criteria: A skill never has to spend a turn fetching what the system already knows.
features.qa_tests: The injected value is current at invocation rather than at spawn. A skill whose injection fails still runs — a failed injection costs its own effect and nothing else.

stories.title: Inject live state into the high-traffic skills first
stories.description: Step 5 of the order: the briefings, sitrep and orchestrator.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A briefing knows today's date and events without asking.
stories.qa_tests: The injected date is the invocation's date, not the session's start. A failed injection does not fail the skill.

stories.title: Inject git and diff state into the code skills
stories.description: code-genius, code-review-genius, master-code-review, update-documentation and tool-creator.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A review skill knows what changed without being told.
stories.qa_tests: The injected diff stat matches the working tree at invocation.

stories.title: Pre-fetch retrieval results for the memory and report skills
stories.description: x-ai-lurker seeded from a memory retrieval, and semantic-memory-save with its similarity results already in hand.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The skill starts with its candidates.
stories.qa_tests: The similarity results present at skill start match a direct query.

features.title: Bundle deterministic scripts
features.description: Steps that do not need model reasoning — they need deterministic execution.
features.requirements: Five candidates: agent-logs gets a log scanner doing pattern match and severity filter; check-reminders gets a firing script that queries due reminders and sends them atomically; mermaid-diagram-creator gets a validator wrapping the CLI and returning pass or fail; sync-discord-slash-commands gets a sync script against the Discord API; and memory-manager gets a manifest writer.
features.acceptance_criteria: The script is deterministic and the model handles only the judgment around it.
features.qa_tests: Each script produces the same output for the same input across runs. The reminder firing is atomic, so a crash between query and send does not double-send or drop. A script carried inside the skill directory travels with the skill; one in a shared scripts folder does not and is how a skill arrives broken.

stories.title: Bundle the five deterministic scripts inside their skill directories
stories.description: Log scanning, reminder firing, mermaid validation, Discord command sync and manifest writing. Inside the skill directory, because a skill is a directory and the sync copies all of it.
stories.requirements: Atomic where it matters — the reminder firing in particular.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Deterministic, and travelling with the skill.
stories.qa_tests: Same input, same output, across runs. The reminder script does not double-send or drop on a crash between query and send. A script placed in a shared folder rather than the skill directory fails to travel, which is the packaging trap.

features.title: Progressive disclosure for dense skills
features.description: SKILL.md stays lean; detail moves to referenced files loaded only when needed. Applies to any skill over roughly 200 lines.
features.requirements: Eight candidates with their extraction targets: code-genius's retry and error-handling detail; code-review-genius's nine-dimension framework; master-code-review's language detection logic; orchestrator's pipeline step detail; planning-genius's codebase exploration procedure; tool-creator's two tool-creation procedures, stateless and stateful; the nightly session's task descriptions, schedules and success criteria; and create-data-class's format reference.
features.acceptance_criteria: The lean SKILL.md is enough to start, and the detail is there when it is needed.
features.qa_tests: The skill works from its lean file alone for the common path. The referenced file is reachable from the skill directory — a reference to a path outside it does not travel with the skill.

stories.title: Split the eight dense skills into lean files plus references
stories.description: Each extraction target named in the source. The referenced files live inside the skill directory so they travel with it.
stories.requirements: Reachable from within the skill directory.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The common path works from the lean file.
stories.qa_tests: The skill completes its common path without loading the detail file. The detail file is reachable when needed. A reference pointing outside the skill directory fails to travel.

features.title: Multi-mind skill patterns
features.description: Last in the order, coordinated with the upstream-minds work, since multi-mind only matters once the containerised minds are on the shared nervous system.
features.requirements: Mind-scoped skills: an allowed-minds frontmatter field so some skills only run for specific minds — one mind owning infrastructure skills, another owning research skills. Inter-mind delegation via fork: one mind delegates to another using context: fork with a mind_id parameter, so a receiving mind determines another is better suited, spawns it as a forked subagent, gets the result back and synthesises a response — and the fork context prevents the infinite response loop, because the delegate's output returns as data rather than as a message that triggers a new response cycle. Mind-aware memory skills: knowledge-graph-save and semantic-memory-save automatically tag writes with the invoking mind_id, so ownership is captured at write time without the caller passing it explicitly. And a consensus pattern for high-stakes decisions: an orchestrator forks several minds, collects their independent outputs and synthesises a consensus, with each fork isolated so no mind sees another's reasoning until synthesis.
features.acceptance_criteria: A delegated task returns as data rather than triggering a response loop, and a memory write always carries the right mind's identity.
features.qa_tests: The mind_id on a write is the UUID rather than the short name, verified by inspecting a freshly-captured row — a write carrying another mind's identity is the failure that made Hex answer as Ada. The consensus pattern's isolation is testable: a mind's output must not contain another's reasoning.

stories.title: Add allowed-minds frontmatter for mind-scoped skills
stories.description: So some skills only run for specific minds.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A mind not listed cannot invoke the skill.
stories.qa_tests: An unlisted mind's invocation is refused. A listed one's succeeds.

stories.title: Implement inter-mind delegation via fork with a mind_id
stories.description: The fork context prevents the infinite response loop, because the delegate's output returns as data rather than as a message that triggers a new response cycle.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No response loop.
stories.qa_tests: A delegated task's result reaches the delegating mind without triggering a further turn on either side. Without the fork, the loop is the failure.

stories.title: Tag memory writes with the invoking mind_id automatically
stories.description: knowledge-graph-save and semantic-memory-save capture ownership at write time without the caller passing it.
stories.requirements: The UUID, never the short name.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A write always carries the writing mind's identity.
stories.qa_tests: Inspect a freshly-captured row: mind_id is the UUID. A write carrying another mind's identity is the failure that made Hex answer as Ada.

stories.title: Build the consensus pattern
stories.description: An orchestrator forks several minds, collects independent outputs and synthesises. Each fork is isolated so no mind sees another's reasoning until synthesis.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Independent outputs, then one synthesis.
stories.qa_tests: Each forked mind's output contains no trace of another's reasoning. The synthesis references all of them. Judged by reading, since the value is in independence rather than in a return code.

features.title: Dynamic web content
features.description: Three horizons for what a mind publishes to the web. Currently the canvas renders a single markdown file that a mind writes to during conversations, with diagrams rendered client-side.
features.requirements: Near-term, full dynamic pages: support multiple canvas files so any file a mind writes to the canvas directory becomes a page automatically — the existing subpath route already does this, and the canvas route just needs to become a subpath route with an index as the default. Medium-term, interactive HTML generation: a skill bundling a script that takes a graph query or dataset, generates a full interactive HTML file, writes it to a static directory and returns the URL, so a mind can publish a live family graph, a system architecture diagram with clickable nodes, or a memory network explorer as standalone pages. Long-term, the mind's own site: a dedicated subdomain rather than a page on Daniel's personal brand site, because the architectural mismatch is real, a mind's outputs deserve their own space, a separate site can carry its own visual identity consistently, and it could be published as a static site built by the mind and deployed via CI. Proposed stack: the same FastAPI pattern, or a static site generator, on the same server, routed at its own subdomain.
features.acceptance_criteria: A mind can publish a page without anyone wiring a route for it.
features.qa_tests: A file written to the canvas directory is served at its path with no code change. A generated interactive page loads and its interactivity works. Note the backlog itself has since moved to the owner site served live from a bind-mounted directory, which is the same pattern this proposes.

stories.title: Make the canvas route a subpath route with an index default
stories.description: Any file written to the canvas directory becomes a page automatically. The existing subpath route already does this.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A new file is served without a code change.
stories.qa_tests: A file written to the directory is served at its path. The default index still serves at the bare route.

stories.title: Add a visualisation skill that generates interactive HTML
stories.description: Takes a graph query or dataset, generates a full interactive HTML file, writes it to the static directory and returns the URL.
stories.requirements: A bundled script inside the skill directory.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A mind can publish a live visualisation and hand over a link.
stories.qa_tests: A generated page loads and its interactivity works. The returned URL resolves.

stories.title: Decide on a separate site for a mind's outputs
stories.description: A dedicated subdomain rather than a page on Daniel's personal brand site. The canvas sitting on a personal brand site is an architectural mismatch.
stories.requirements: A decision, and a stack if yes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Either a site or a recorded reason to keep the canvas where it is.
stories.qa_tests: Not code. The artifact is the decision.
